content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, minimum spend, take-or-pay or shortfall mechanic binding AP:

- **§5 Fees and Payment (p0023)** is a pure revenue share on actual auction activity ("The Parties agree to share any revenue generated as a result of this Agreement"). AP pays nothing absent usage; its only payment obligation is applicable sales/use taxes.
- **§1 (p0001)** expressly disclaims exclusivity and confirms the Agreement "will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties" — no volume caps or channel restrictions on us.
- The "minimum" hits are benign or in our favour: **p0014** defines Winning Bid Price as no less than AP's own agreed floor price; **p0062** merely disclaims any guaranteed minimum revenue (a Vendor-side disclaimer, not an AP commitment).
- The **§4(a) Initial Term lock-in** (no termination during year one except for breach) constrains exit but creates no purchase or volume obligation, so it sits under the termination rule rather than this one.

One watch item: commercial Exhibits are referenced but not exposed in this document. If an Exhibit introduces a minimum spend or volume floor, we should push it to the fallback — commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
